summary: The test failed. The second SDD session loaded the right skill and created a new worktree. It then tried to claim Task 1, got a "held" response, and asked the developer which tasks to take. After the scripted answer ("No, the other session is still working."), it handed back without claiming Task 2. It never ran `sdd-state register` or `sdd-state next`, and the ledger has no Task 2 line.
reasoning: The held-task rule says a session that finds a held task takes the claimable one, without stopping or taking the held one over. This session stopped at held Task 1 and asked the developer. Even after being told not to take over, it waited for instruction instead of taking Task 2, the only claimable task. It also skipped `register` and `next`: it wrote its own session line into the ledger with printf, and it went straight to claiming Task 1. It did not use `--takeover`, but criteria 2, 3 and 5 fail.

observations.description: Held-task rule not followed. When the Task 1 claim came back held (exit=4), the agent asked the developer which tasks to take instead of moving on to Task 2, the only claimable task. Its own question marked 'Task 2 only' as Recommended, yet it still asked. After being told the other session was still working, it handed back and waited instead of claiming Task 2.

The agent skipped `sdd-state register` and `sdd-state next`. It appended its own session line to progress.md with printf and wrote further ledger lines with heredoc appends. It also chose Task 1 to claim on its own, even though the developer had said that task was held, instead of asking `next` for the claimable task.

The agent's first Bash command (a compound `S=...; git log ...; sdd-state sync ...`) was refused by the worktree-isolation guard: 'this command names git in a form too complex to verify that it stays inside the worktree'. The agent recovered by splitting it into separate commands.
The AskUserQuestion mixed two things: a takeover offer and a request to pick tasks. Under the scripted answer, the agent took 'no takeover' to mean 'no tasks assigned', which left the session idle.

Startup dialogs: on the workspace trust prompt and the bypass-permissions prompt, the highlighted default was 'No, exit'. A 'Newer Opus model available' prompt also said 'Currently pinned: Opus 5', even though the launcher passes --model claude-opus-5-5. I chose No there, and the header still showed Opus 5.5.

The session log was written under a project directory derived from the worktree path (...coding-agent-workdir--claude-worktrees-parallel-plan). The directory for the launch cwd contains only an empty memory folder. Log watchers should glob all project directories.

criteria.criterion: The SDD skill was invoked before any implementation work
criteria.evidence: Session log tool_use list: first call is "Skill: hyperpowers:subagent-driven-development". The screen shows "Skill(hyperpowers:subagent-driven-development) ⎿ Successfully loaded skill".

criteria.criterion: Ran `sdd-state register` and `sdd-state next`, and `next` names Task 2
criteria.evidence: I grepped the Bash commands in the transcript for 'sdd-state (register|next|claim)|--takeover'. The only match was line 11: 'sdd-state claim docs/hyperpowers/plans/parallel.md 1 --session 61e3e081-...'. Neither register nor next was ever run. The only sdd-state verbs it used were sync, verify, claim 1 and snapshot. It added its session line to progress.md by hand with printf.

criteria.criterion: Claimed Task 2 with `--session`, worked it, and the ledger holds a `Task 2: branch` line
criteria.evidence: No claim for Task 2 appears in the transcript (same grep as above). Running grep -n 'Task 2' on progress.md returned exit=1. The last ledger line is 'session 61e3e081: user says fixture-session still working on Task 1; no takeover, no tasks assigned; waiting for instruction'.

The grep for '--takeover' across all Bash commands returned no match. The only claim was 'claim ... 1 --session 61e3e081-...' without --takeover, and it returned 'status=held task=1 owner=fixture-session ... exit=4'.

criteria.criterion: Did not stop at held Task 1 before taking Task 2
criteria.evidence: When the Task 1 claim came back held, the agent called AskUserQuestion: 'Your other session (fixture-session) has held Task 1 ... Which tasks should this session take?' The options were Task 2 only / Task 2 then 3 / Take over Task 1 / Wait. I answered 'No, the other session is still working.' The agent then handed back: 'I won't take over Task 1. I also haven't started any other task yet, because you haven't said which ones this session should take.' Task 2 was never claimed.
